notes: Every check is binary. The lesson ships only if ALL checks pass. 'code' checks are deterministic Python; 'llm' checks are judged by a separate LLM call that must quote evidence.

checks.description: All required sections exist, in teaching order: What is it -> Why it matters -> How it works -> Worked example -> Key words -> Recap -> Check your understanding.
Lesson body is between 700 and 2000 words: long enough to teach, short enough to finish in one sitting (~10-12 min).
Average sentence length <= 16 words and no sentence longer than 30 words. Long sentences are the #1 barrier for readers with limited English.
Flesch Reading Ease >= 55 on the prose (glossary terms excluded), i.e. roughly 'plain English'.
None of the words on the hard-vocabulary blocklist (e.g. utilize, leverage, paradigm, facilitate, plethora) appear.
Every technical term from the jargon list that is used in the lesson also appears in the 'Key words' section.
'Check your understanding' has at least 3 questions and gives an answer for each.
No statement contradicts the reference facts, and none of the listed misconceptions (M1-M4) is stated as true.

Every specific factual claim (names, dates, numbers, product names, technical claims) is supported by the reference facts. Analogies and the worked example are allowed if clearly presented as illustrations.

Covers ALL of: (a) definition of RAG with the expansion of the acronym, (b) LLM knowledge limits - cut-off date or private data, (c) hallucination, (d) why RAG instead of retraining, (e) the steps chunk -> embed -> store -> retrieve -> augment -> generate, (f) RAG does not change the model's weights, (g) RAG reduces but does not remove errors.
Uses at least one concrete, everyday example familiar to a young person in India, and walks ONE running example through every step of how RAG works (not just mentions it once).
Every technical term is explained in simple words at (or right before) its FIRST use. No term is used before it is explained.

Language suits a 12th-grade graduate from a non-English-medium school: short simple sentences, common words, no idioms or slang, no references that need Western/US cultural knowledge, friendly encouraging tone.
Each section builds on the previous one, there are no forward references to unexplained ideas, no contradictions between sections, and the recap matches what was taught.
Assumes zero background: does not require knowing programming, maths beyond school level, machine learning, or neural networks to follow the lesson.
